clue.text: Cash advance securing cold and hot water in Scotland

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly within, so the loan wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a cash advance is a loan
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A Scottish payday loan seems to come with hot and cold running water.
explanation.definitionFit: A lochan is a small Scottish lake or pond, so a body of water in Scotland.

clue.text: African politician once going over area in Ireland

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over places the politician above the rest

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal, a party that once held power in Britain

indicators.note: in places the area inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A former politician from Africa crosses over to a part of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberian is a native of Liberia, a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Students swap fake finally for a work of art

indicators.note: swap signals one letter exchanged for another within the word
for gives what the letter is exchanged for

parts.note: a college is a body of students
fake finally is the last letter of fake

explanation.surface: Students exchange a forgery at the last minute for a genuine artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake finally' is the last letter of fake, E, which 'swap ... for' replaces with A.
explanation.definitionFit: A collage is a work of art made by sticking assorted materials onto a backing.

clue.text: Successful applicant makes a mark with ease, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase before it is spoken out loud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: a point, a mark, followed by E's, the plural of the letter E, run together when spoken

explanation.surface: A job applicant scores with apparent ease.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'a point E's' (a mark plus more than one E) sounds like the answer. 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointee is someone given a post, so the applicant who got the job.

clue.text: Mulishness of old theologian about to leave church office

parts.note: BD, Bachelor of Divinity, is a theology degree, so a theologian

indicators.note: to leave says a piece departs, so that letter is dropped from the church office

parts.note: a curacy is the office of a curate in the church
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric stubbornly refuses to give up his parish post.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulishness is stubbornness like a mule's, and obduracy is hard-hearted stubbornness: synonyms.

clue.text: How similar bargains may be secured, moreover?

definitions.text: How similar bargains may be secured
definitions.meaning: bargains bought with the same voucher or coupon, read literally
moreover means in addition, for the same reason

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning moreover or likewise, and literally describes paying with one identical token.

clue.text: High-class pundit's employment

parts.note: U is a British label for upper-class speech and manners
a sage is a wise person, a pundit

explanation.surface: A posh commentator has found a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means the way something is used, its employment.

clue.text: Maid in house heard sound of force eight wind

indicators.note: heard sound of says the phrase is said out loud, giving words spelt differently

parts.note: force eight on the Beaufort scale is a gale, so a big gale

explanation.surface: A housemaid listens to the howl of a severe gale.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a dated word for a lady's maid, after a waiting-woman in the Bible.

clue.text: Not ready, somehow, to withdraw TA further in that direction

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are jumbled in some unspecified way

parts.note: the fodder words, from which TA is taken before rearranging

explanation.surface: The Territorial Army is pulled back because it is not ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges NOT READY once 'to withdraw' has removed TA. TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder means over there, at a distance in a direction pointed to.

clue.text: By no means the first journo to be an infiltrator!

definitions.text: By no means the first journo to be an infiltrator!

parts.words: By no means the first journo to be an infiltrator!
parts.note: a journalist who writes a column but is not first in line, say fifth, describes a traitor working within

explanation.definitionFit: A fifth columnist is a member of a hidden group working inside a country for its enemies.

clue.text: Writer's position at end of dance

definitions.note: read as 'Writer is', so the definition is the word writer, a pen

indicators.note: at end of places the position after the dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
a point is a position, as in a point on a map

explanation.surface: A novelist's view of life is summed up at the close of a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' is not possessive: it means 'Writer is'. The writer here is a pen, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint is a pen, so a writing instrument, in a pun on writer as something that writes.

clue.text: A new invention held to be extraneous

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so the invention sits within the other letters

parts.note: a lie is an invention, a made-up story

explanation.surface: A novel invention is deemed to have no bearing on the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien can mean foreign or not belonging, which is what extraneous means.

clue.text: Pragmatic type working as tiler

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A practical person is happy to earn a living laying tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the letters of AS TILER.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is someone who deals with things as they are, a pragmatic sort of person.

clue.text: Raise English tax in general

indicators.note: in places the tax inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
VAT, value added tax, is a British sales tax

explanation.surface: A call to put up English taxes across the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads as 'overall', but 'in' is a container signal and the general is the Confederate commander Robert E Lee.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to lift or raise something up: synonyms.

clue.text: Expert tending to carry keys

indicators.note: to carry means to hold within, so the keys go inside

parts.note: apt means tending or inclined to
D and E are musical keys

explanation.surface: A specialist is inclined to carry a bunch of keys around.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means skilled or expert: a straight synonym.

clue.text: Porter talked of mess where nuts are stored

indicators.note: talked of says the porter's name is said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Cole Porter was an American songwriter
a hole is a mess or fix, as in 'in a hole'

explanation.surface: A hotel porter speaks of a disgraceful place where nuts are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' is not a doorman but the songwriter Cole Porter, whose first name sounds like coal. Nuts here are small lumps of coal.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalhole is a cellar or bunker for coal, and nuts are small lumps of coal.

clue.text: Man and woman digesting paper's misleading statement

indicators.note: digesting means taking inside, so the paper goes into the names

parts.note: Hal is a man's name
Ruth is a woman's name
the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A couple read the newspaper and come away with a misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-truth is a statement only partly true, made to mislead.

clue.text: Dancer's control over rising English film director?

definitions.note: read as 'Dancer is'; Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

indicators.note: in a down entry, over places the control above the rest

parts.note: a rein controls a horse

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Carol Reed was an English film director, of The Third Man

explanation.surface: A dancer controls an English film director's rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancer' is not a performer but one of Santa's reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancer is named among Santa's reindeer in the poem A Visit from St Nicholas.

clue.text: Wake-up call from priest endlessly keen to limit wickedness

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a priest's title

indicators.note: to limit means to enclose or bound, so the wickedness sits within
endlessly means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: ill as a noun means evil or wickedness

explanation.surface: A cleric eager to curb sin issues a morning call to rouse the faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager, but it is fodder: 'endlessly' strips its ends, and 'to limit' wraps the two inner letters round the wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning, a wake-up call.

clue.text: Attractive female's rejected craft work

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so the letter goes from the word

parts.note: fetching means attractive
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A pretty woman has had her handiwork turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made by a craft process of acid on metal.

clue.text: Left university career oddly showing monetary gain

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Someone quit a university career, apparently for the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or profit, often with a hint of disapproval, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: European stars seen around Sulawesi once

indicators.note: seen around means the stars enclose the other letter

parts.note: celebs are celebrities, stars

explanation.surface: A European is spotted surrounded by celebrities on an Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebes was the former name of Sulawesi, an island of Indonesia.

clue.text: High jinks involving learner, one in short dress

indicators.note: in places the learner and the one inside the dress
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a frock is a dress
L is the learner sign on a British car
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A learner gets up to fun and games in a skimpy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes FROCK down to FROC, with L and I put 'in' it. 'involving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic is a bout of playful fun, as are high jinks.

clue.text: Get back engineers connected with mining area

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army
a claim is a plot of land staked out for mining

explanation.surface: Engineers try to recover a disused mine.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim is to recover or take back what was yours: synonyms.

clue.text: Patois a Republican understood

parts.note: got means understood, as in 'I got it'

explanation.surface: A Republican understood the local dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or slang of a group, a kind of patois.

clue.text: Bunting taken from door to landing

indicators.note: taken from says the letters are lifted out of a run of the clue's words

explanation.surface: Festive flags have been removed from the doorway to the landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' looks like festive flags, but here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European bird of the bunting family, once eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Prone, possibly, to be mendacious

definitions.meaning: prone means stretched out face down; 'possibly' says this is one way of resting flat

explanation.definitionFit: Lying means both stretched out flat, as prone is, and telling falsehoods, as the mendacious do.

clue.text: It's not even unfair ignoring it

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving something out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: inequitable means unfair or unjust

explanation.surface: Something is called uneven and unjust when one overlooks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link: the definition is 'not even'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequable means uneven or not uniform, so not even.

clue.text: Ponder fellow soldier's note about army

indicators.note: about here means next to, placing the note beside the army

parts.note: CO is a prefix meaning joint or fellow, as in co-worker
GI is an American soldier
TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve army
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A comrade in arms writes a short memo concerning the army.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply, which is to ponder: synonyms.

clue.text: Another drink for Yellow-Dog Dingo?

definitions.meaning: a second drink taken after the first, such as a beer after a spirit
in Kipling's Just So Stories Yellow-Dog Dingo pursues Old Man Kangaroo across Australia

explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken after another, and one who pursues, as Kipling's dingo pursues the kangaroo.
